definitions.explanation: An involuntary trembling of the body caused by cold, fear, excitement, or strong emotion. Can describe both physical shivering and an emotional response.

examples.japanese: {寒|さむ}さで{身震|みぶる}いした。
{恐|おそ}ろしい{話|はなし}を{聞|き}いて{身震|みぶる}いした。
examples.english: I shuddered upon hearing the terrifying story.

examples.japanese: {初|はじ}めてオーケストラの{生|なま}{演奏|えんそう}を{聴|き}いたとき、{感動|かんどう}で{身震|みぶる}いするほどだった。
examples.english: When I heard a live orchestra for the first time, I was so moved that I shuddered.

notes:
Compound of {身|み} (body) + {震|ふる}い (shaking), with rendaku changing ふ to ぶ. Functions as both a noun and a する verb.

Unlike {震|ふる}える (to tremble), which describes sustained shaking, {身震|みぶる}い typically refers to a sudden, involuntary shudder — a brief whole-body reaction.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {身震|みぶる}いする (to shudder)
- {身震|みぶる}いがする (to feel a shudder)
- {身震|みぶる}いするほど (enough to make one shudder)
- {恐怖|きょうふ}で{身震|みぶる}いする (to shudder with fear)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {震|ふる}える: to tremble, to shake (sustained trembling)
- {鳥肌|とりはだ}: goosebumps (a related physical reaction)
- {武者震|むしゃぶる}い: trembling with excitement before action (anticipatory)
